derived.label: U.S. total auto jobs (manufacturing + dealers)
derived.note: Sum of motor vehicles and parts manufacturing and motor vehicle and parts dealers, two disjoint payroll industries. This defined total excludes automotive repair, wholesale and other auto-related employment. Normalize each input to people before adding, on common observation dates only.

notes.units: The units field describes raw FRED observations. Multiply each raw observation by multiplier exactly once. Derived employment series sum components after scaling to people, with no additional conversion.
notes.employment: Employment levels and changes are payroll jobs, not unique workers. Manufacturing subsets overlap the manufacturing total; do not add parent industries to their subsets.
notes.regionalCoverage: The selected states are Michigan, Ohio, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania and Minnesota. They are not a complete Midwest region; Pennsylvania is outside the Census Midwest.
notes.retailPrices: Average retail prices are published NSA and describe actual prices for the stated quantities. CPI indexes are better suited to measuring inflation because product composition and quality can change over time.
notes.gdp: Quarterly real GDP can be compared using percentage changes or a shared base-quarter index, not raw national-currency levels. Q1 2021 and Q1 2025 are quarter baselines, not January observations; any monthly equivalent growth rate is a calculation, not monthly GDP.
notes.conflictBaseline: The user selected February 28, 2026. Use each series last observed value strictly before that date; report each actual baseline date. February 28 is a Saturday, so daily market series normally use February 27 and weekly fuel series the preceding Monday. Describe changes since the baseline, not causal effects of the war.
